title: Difference Between Standard and Volumetric Weight
body_markdown:
It can come as surprise when packages you consider light and soft weigh more than those you consider heavy. This is because not all weight is created equal. The light items could take up a lot of space and hinder carriers from shipping other products.


In this post, we explain the difference between standard weight and volumetric weight.


**What is standard weight?**


Standard weight, also known as physical weight, is the weight of an item according to the scale. It is calculated by weighing items using a scale as simple as a bathroom scale.


**What is volumetric weight?**


Volumetric weight, also known as dimensional weight, is calculated when items are packaged in boxes or anything that has shape. It is calculated with a formula using the volume weight of a package based on the actual dimensions of the box.


Volumetric weight is a necessity because it helps shipping companies maintain their stellar service. It ensures a fair charge for merchants shipping large but very light items that take up more space than a package that is small but very heavy.


**How is volumetric weight calculated?**


Volumetric weight is gotten using the following formula: Length x Width x Height. It means that the larger a parcel is, the larger its volumetric weight will be and vice versa. This is why the volumetric weight of a shipment can only be calculated when the length, width and height of the package is known.
